title: Canary Deployment and Automatic Rollback
prompt: Route 10% of traffic for the production Lambda alias to the new version only during the initial monitoring interval. If the interval completes, proceed to full traffic; if an error-rate alarm fires, roll back to the previous version without human intervention.

choices.text: Update all traffic to the new version, then notify the on-call engineer
choices.explanation: This provides neither validation under partial load nor automatic rollback.

choices.text: Change only the new version's reserved concurrency
choices.explanation: This does not manage the traffic split or rollback to the previous version.

choices.text: Manually configure weighted routing on the Lambda alias and connect the alarm to an email notification
choices.explanation: This supports a partial rollout but does not provide automatic promotion and rollback.

choices.text: Configure a Lambda canary deployment and automatic rollback with CodeDeploy
choices.explanation: This supports a staged rollout through a weighted alias and alarm integration.

learning.reason: This supports a staged rollout through a weighted alias and alarm integration.
learning.concept: Choose deployment alarms that indicate the health of the change, such as the user error rate.

title: Deployment Across Many Accounts
prompt: Automatically deploy audit resources to new accounts that join the Security OU. Apply the same definitions to existing accounts as well; manual role creation during account initialization is not possible.

choices.text: Manually create the same stack in each account
choices.explanation: Future accounts will not receive the deployment automatically.

choices.text: Configure an AWS Config aggregator for the organization
choices.explanation: This provides visibility but does not deploy the specified CloudFormation resources.

choices.text: Create an organization trail in CloudTrail
choices.explanation: This centralizes operation records but does not deploy templates.

choices.text: Configure automatic deployment with Organizations-integrated service-managed StackSets
choices.explanation: This manages deployment to accounts added to the target OU.

learning.reason: This manages deployment to accounts added to the target OU.
learning.concept: Before deployment, check the target OUs, Regions, concurrency settings, and failure tolerance.

title: Scheduled AMI Updates
prompt: Rebuild a shared AMI every week and replicate only versions that pass configuration tests to multiple Regions. Avoid relying on manual patching of existing EC2 instances to patch the baseline OS.

choices.text: Increase the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling group
choices.explanation: This changes the number of running instances but does not update the AMI contents.

choices.text: Build an image creation, testing, and distribution pipeline with EC2 Image Builder
choices.explanation: This manages recurring updates to the base image.

choices.text: Manually patch only the running EC2 instances
choices.explanation: The AMI used by new EC2 instances remains unchanged unless it is updated separately.

choices.text: Distribute snapshots of running EC2 instances every week
choices.explanation: This replicates storage but does not integrate controlled image creation, testing, and distribution.

learning.reason: This manages recurring updates to the base image.
learning.concept: Manage updates to existing instances separately from updates to the base image used when instances are recreated.

title: Triggering Automatic Remediation
prompt: Periodically evaluate existing S3 buckets for deviations from a required encryption setting, and automatically run an approved remediation procedure when a bucket is noncompliant. Do not treat the absence of a change API call as proof of compliance.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to capture only new bucket creations
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate existing buckets or deviations that occur after creation.

choices.text: Combine an AWS Config rule with remediation using Systems Manager Automation
choices.explanation: A compliance evaluation can trigger the defined remediation.

choices.text: Set only a billing alarm
choices.explanation: A change in charges cannot determine whether a bucket configuration is noncompliant.

choices.text: Review CloudTrail history periodically
choices.explanation: This tracks operations but does not perform remediation.

learning.reason: A compliance evaluation can trigger the defined remediation.
learning.concept: Limit remediation permissions to the required resources and operations, and preserve consistency if the procedure runs more than once.

title: Reducing Notifications with a Composite Alarm
prompt: CPU utilization and the application error rate are evaluated in separate windows, and each already has an alarm. Send the on-call team one notification only when both are in ALARM, while preserving each alarm’s evaluation criteria.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch composite alarm with an AND condition for the ALARM states of both alarms
choices.explanation: It can combine the states of individual alarms for notification.

choices.text: Connect both individual alarms directly to the same SNS topic
choices.explanation: A threshold breach in either alarm alone would send a notification.

choices.text: Monitor the average of the two values with a new alarm
choices.explanation: The values have different units, and their average does not represent the logical AND of the existing alarm states.

choices.text: Only extend the metric retention period
choices.explanation: This does not affect how notification conditions are combined.

learning.reason: The states of individual alarms can be combined for notification.
learning.concept: When individual alarms have different evaluation periods, also check when their ALARM states overlap.

title: Detecting Failed Deployments in ECS
prompt: A service uses the standard ECS rolling update deployment. A new task exits soon after startup and never reaches a steady state. You want to return to the last successful deployment without adding custom monitoring scripts.

choices.text: Only extend the health check grace period
choices.explanation: This can help with temporary initialization delays, but it does not automatically restore the previous version when a failure persists.

choices.text: Only increase the number of containers and continue
choices.explanation: The startup failure remains, and this does not configure a return to the previous deployment.

choices.text: Shorten the image deletion policy
choices.explanation: This controls retention of build artifacts; it does not roll back after a startup failure.

choices.text: Enable rollback for the ECS deployment circuit breaker
choices.explanation: It can detect a failed deployment and return to the previous healthy deployment.

learning.reason: It can detect a failed deployment and return to the previous healthy deployment.
learning.concept: Design detection both for startup failures and for patterns where application metrics deteriorate after startup.

title: Build the Artifact Once
prompt: The container contents differed between development and production after approval. You want to promote the tested binary and deploy that same binary to production, even if a shared tag is moved to point elsewhere.

choices.text: Use the image digest after the build as the pipeline artifact, and update the production task definition with that same digest
choices.explanation: This identifies the tested contents without relying on a mutable tag.

choices.text: Add a timestamp to the tag just before the production deployment
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that the digest points to the same content that was tested.

choices.text: Pull latest in each environment and deploy to test first
choices.explanation: The tag could move while approval is pending.

choices.text: Rebuild the same commit for production
choices.explanation: Updates to the base image or external dependencies can produce a different artifact.

learning.reason: This identifies the tested contents without relying on a mutable tag.
learning.concept: Promote the immutable identifier of the inspected artifact, not the name of the source.

title: Recovery Exercise During a Regional Outage
prompt: The DR environment is tested monthly, but production traffic must not be affected. Automate the process from restoring business data through validating the application in an isolated environment. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Switch production weighted DNS to 100% on a monthly basis
choices.explanation: This affects customer traffic.

choices.text: Overwrite the existing production database with a backup
choices.explanation: This affects production data and service.

choices.text: Restore from backups in the DR Region into an isolated environment, then use a Runbook to verify consistency and recovery time
choices.explanation: This tests the actual restoration procedure without touching the existing service.

choices.text: Only check monthly that the backup job succeeded
choices.explanation: This does not measure restoration time or verify that the system works after recovery.

learning.reason: This tests the actual restoration procedure without touching the existing service.
learning.concept: Measure successful backup creation separately from successful restoration within the target time.

title: Pinning the Artifact During Approval
prompt: Multiple commits pass through the same pipeline. An approver wants to promote a build that has already been tested to production. Which design prevents the approved artifact from being confused with a new artifact generated while approval is pending?

choices.text: Rebuild the same branch in production
choices.explanation: A different commit or different dependencies might be used.

choices.text: Approve a mutable latest tag
choices.explanation: It might point to different content after approval.

choices.text: Bind the execution ID and artifact digest to the approval record, then refer to the same digest during promotion
choices.explanation: The approved artifact and the artifact actually promoted match.

choices.text: Have the approver record only the time
choices.explanation: This does not uniquely identify the artifact.

learning.reason: The approved artifact and the artifact actually promoted match.
learning.concept: Bind approval to the execution's contents and promote the artifact between environments without rebuilding it.

title: Centralized Notifications for Release Failures
prompt: Multiple teams deploy with CodePipeline. You need to notify a central on-call destination immediately when a pipeline fails, without polling, and handle only the relevant pipelines. Which approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Monitor only CloudTrail's StartPipelineExecution
choices.explanation: Recording that an execution started does not reveal its outcome.

choices.text: List execution history every 15 minutes
choices.explanation: This is not the requested event-driven approach.

choices.text: Aggregate only pipeline success emails
choices.explanation: This cannot provide immediate notifications of failures.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to filter for FAILED pipeline execution state changes and send them to SNS
choices.explanation: This provides event-driven notifications filtered by pipeline and state, with a centrally managed destination.

learning.reason: This provides event-driven notifications filtered by pipeline and state, with a centrally managed destination.
learning.concept: An audit event recording that an operation was initiated differs from a state event reporting the outcome of a long-running operation.
